There would be no industrial revolution without the black death , those 7 years changed the face of the continent and were a big blow to feudalism. Areas not (very much or at all) affected by the plague remained agrarian and backwards till the 19th century .

The world ( or rather big and important chunks of it ) has been ruled by different people through different times , what we live in the last few centuries will be only a chapter in history.

Persian empire ruled the "known world" for centuries

The Mongols , enough said

Ming China

Mauryas of India

The Sumerians , probably the first empire

The Ottomans

Umayyad Caliphate

Most ( Umayyads excluded) of those big state entities included lots of different peoples with different perspectives . Now if you wanna talk specifically about Europe it was always a densely populated continent with no natural obstacles and very diverse in cultures languages and ways . Overpopulation quickly depleted resources and drove many into banditry and piracy, the pirates pioneered exploration while constant warfare advanced military technology and the small size of realms prevented states from stagnating ( which was the case of China ).

The breaking point was Ottoman conquest of the Balkans which made possible for all the stored knowledge of the east to be transported into west bringing humanism ( the main European characteristic ) , stating renaissance and the whole debate about the place of man into the world.

*This is my personal view, a real historian will know better .

Essentially the environment was best suited to the long term development of western civilization. Good climate, soil and natural wealth. China also could have ruled to world as it was suited environmentally too but their centralism and unity was actually a negative since a short sighted emperor could isolate China from the world stage. At one point in the Ming dynasty China had the most powerful navy in the world but a short sighted emperor disbanded it. Europe was not united and thus there was much more competition and European nations had the advantage in taking care of lesser advanced people through colonization. Zheng He could only go to China, Columbus went to Genoa, England, Portugal before finally being financed and supported by Spain. China had the capacity to colonize (and maybe discover, although that's about luck) the America but they lacked the will due to their culture and idea of world order. For most of history China was the most powerful country. Seeing the rise of China and the rest of Asia along with the relative decline of the west makes me think we are returning to the status quo of the years gone by.
